name: Java
summary: Learn Java program structure, classes, collections, exceptions, streams, and file APIs.

lessons.title: Program entry and types
lessons.explanation: A simple Java app starts in public static void main(String[] args). Declare the type of each variable. Primitive types such as int hold values. Reference variables such as String refer to objects. Save the public class below as Main.java.

api.name: System.out.println()
api.description: Write a value followed by a line break.

api.name: Integer.parseInt(text)
api.description: Convert decimal text to an int, or throw NumberFormatException.

api.name: String.length()
api.description: Count UTF-16 code units in a string.

lessons.practice: Add a second item and print the combined total.
lessons.pitfall: When comparing String contents, use equals. The == operator tests reference identity for objects.

lessons.title: Control flow and arrays
lessons.explanation: Use if and else to choose branches. Use for-each to traverse every element or an index-based for loop when positions matter. Arrays have a fixed length and start at index zero.

api.name: array.length
api.description: Read the fixed length of an array.

api.name: Arrays.sort(array)
api.description: Sort an array in place using java.util.Arrays.

api.name: break / continue
api.description: Exit a loop or skip the remainder of its current iteration.

lessons.practice: Find the largest element in a nonempty array. Test with all-negative input.
lessons.pitfall: The last valid array index is length minus one.

lessons.title: Methods, constructors, and interfaces
lessons.explanation: Methods give an operation a name, parameters, and a return type. A constructor initializes a new object. An interface gives callers a shared contract while classes provide the implementation.

api.name: new Class(...)
api.description: Create an object and run its constructor.

api.name: this
api.description: Refer to the current instance.

api.name: @Override
api.description: Ask the compiler to confirm a method implements or overrides an existing declaration.

lessons.practice: Add another class implementing Described. Store both implementations in a Described array and print each label.
lessons.pitfall: A static method has no this reference. Pass an instance when it needs instance state.

lessons.title: Lists, sets, and maps
lessons.explanation: List preserves sequence, Set keeps unique values, and Map looks up values by key. Declare the interface type where possible. Generics specify which object types a collection can hold.

api.name: ArrayList.add(value)
api.description: Append an item to a growable list.

api.name: HashSet.contains(value)
api.description: Test set membership.

api.name: Map.getOrDefault(key, fallback)
api.description: Read a map entry or use the fallback when the key is absent.

api.name: Map.merge(key, value, function)
api.description: Add a new value or combine it with an existing one.

lessons.practice: Count the frequency of three words and print the count for a missing word.
lessons.pitfall: List.of creates an unmodifiable list. Use an ArrayList when you need to add or remove entries.

lessons.title: Exceptions and resource lifetimes
lessons.explanation: Catch the specific failures you can handle. A checked exception such as IOException must be caught or declared. Try-with-resources closes an AutoCloseable object even if the block exits early.

api.name: try (resource) { ... }
api.description: Tie resource cleanup to the block scope.

api.name: throw
api.description: Raise an exception at the point of failure.

api.name: throws IOException
api.description: Tell the caller a checked exception can propagate.

lessons.practice: Change the line to a word and confirm that your numeric conversion fails gracefully.
lessons.pitfall: Avoid empty catch blocks. They hide information the caller or developer needs.

lessons.title: Streams, lambdas, and Optional
lessons.explanation: A stream pipeline can filter and transform a collection before consuming it. Operations such as filter and map are lazy. Terminal operations such as count or toList start traversal.

api.name: Stream.filter(predicate)
api.description: Keep values satisfying a test.

api.name: Stream.map(function)
api.description: Transform each value.

api.name: Stream.findFirst()
api.description: Return an Optional with the first element, when present.

api.name: Optional.orElse(fallback)
api.description: Return the wrapped value or a default.

lessons.practice: Find the first label of length four and display a fallback if it is missing. Use Java 16 or newer for Stream.toList.
lessons.pitfall: A stream cannot be reused after its terminal operation. Create another stream from the source.

lessons.title: Paths, files, and dates
lessons.explanation: Path represents a filesystem path. Files provides operations on paths. java.time types represent calendar dates and time values without exposing mutable date fields.

api.name: Path.of(parts...)
api.description: Construct a Path from one or more strings.

api.name: Files.readString() / Files.writeString()
api.description: Read or write a small UTF-8 text file.

api.name: LocalDate.parse(text)
api.description: Parse an ISO-8601 calendar date.

lessons.practice: Write a date one month later, then read the date back. Use Java 11 or newer for the file methods.
lessons.pitfall: LocalDate has no timezone or time of day. Use an Instant or a suitable zoned type when you need a moment on the timeline.
